newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Millon to visit U.S. on NATO row.
newsitem.headline: France's Millon to visit U.S. on NATO row.

text.p: After months of deadlock, French Defence Minister Charles Millon visits the United States on Monday and may return with a face-saving deal over President Jacques Chirac's drive to win a bigger role for Europe in commanding NATO.

The dispute between the two allies has compounded NATO's reform headaches as it seeks to defuse Russian President Boris Yeltsin's opposition to NATO plans to expand into eastern and central Europe after the Cold War.

Millon will travel to Washington for talks with U.S. Defence Secretary William Cohen on France's demands, which focus on naming a European officer to take charge of NATO's southern command based in Naples, Italy, which has always been held by an American.

"I will...explain to him again the French, European, position that there should be a parity of responsibilities between Europeans and Americans," Millon said. "I think we must renounce all predominance and choose a true alliance."
Washington has flatly ruled out yielding the command, which controls the Mediterranean and access to the Balkans, North Africa and the Middle East.

But a NATO official said that prospects for a broader compromise between the two allies have brightened after months of discord. "There is no guarantee of a deal at the moment, but now we are cautiously optimistic," he said.

Current solutions could involve giving France command over a new rapid reaction force for the Mediterranean and a new headquarters of a sub-region -- but not the prized southern command itself, the official said.

The stakes are high for France, which has said it will freeze its planned return to NATO's military command after three decades unless Washington yields to give Europeans a greater say in their defence after the Cold War.
"France has always been very clear," Millon told Europe 1 radio. "If there is no progress on this point, France will remain at its current status."
"But we expect that we can reach points of accord after discussions and dialogue with our American friends," he said.

The French say the Europeans should run the southern region because Americans hold both NATO strategic commands, the Supreme Allied Commander in Europe based in Belgium and the Supreme Atlantic Commander in Virginia.
Washington says that it has the biggest military capability in the region, notably the nuclear-armed Sixth Fleet whose commanding admiral traditionally heads AFSOUTH.
The issue is meant to be resolved in time for a July summit in Madrid at which NATO plans to invite former a first group of former Soviet bloc states to join.
Yeltsin faced domestic charges he capitulated on NATO enlargement after his a summit with U.S. President Bill Clinton in Helsinki last week.

While branding any NATO expansion a "serious mistake", Yeltsin agreed to sign a charter building a new relationship with NATO. The two leaders said the summit paved the way to a new security partnership for the 21st century.
